title: 〜かぎりだ
meaning: extremely …; could not be more … (the speaker's own feeling)
simpleExplanation: Emotion adjective + かぎりだ says the speaker feels that emotion to the utmost: 嬉しいかぎりだ "I could not be happier". It is only used for the speaker's own present feeling and only with a small set of emotion words. It is not the same かぎり as "as long as" (限り).
whenUsed: Formal speeches, letters, thank-you messages, and polite written comments. In casual speech people say 本当に嬉しい or 嬉しくてたまらない instead.
formation: い-adjective + かぎりだ (嬉しい・寂しい・羨ましい・心強い・悔しい)
な-adjective + な + かぎりだ (残念なかぎりだ)
Noun + の + かぎりだ (光栄のかぎりです)

examples.ja: 長年の夢がかなって、嬉しいかぎりだ。
examples.reading: ながねんのゆめがかなって、うれしいかぎりだ。
examples.en: My long-held dream has come true; I could not be happier.
examples.note: The speaker's own joy about a fulfilled dream.

examples.ja: 親友が遠くへ引っ越してしまい、寂しいかぎりです。
examples.reading: しんゆうがとおくへひっこししてしまい、さびしいかぎりです。
examples.en: My best friend moved far away, and I feel terribly lonely.
examples.note: Loneliness after a friend's move; ですます form for a letter.

examples.ja: こんな大役を任せていただき、光栄のかぎりです。
examples.reading: こんなたいやくをまかせていただき、こうえいのかぎりです。
examples.en: I am deeply honored to be entrusted with such an important role.
examples.note: 光栄のかぎり: noun + の, the standard phrase for accepting an honour.

examples.ja: 皆様に温かく迎えていただき、心強いかぎりです。
examples.reading: みなさまにあたたかくむかえていただき、こころづよいかぎりです。
examples.en: Being so warmly welcomed by you all, I feel greatly reassured.
examples.note: 心強い is one of the most frequent partners.

examples.ja: あと一点で合格だったとは、悔しいかぎりだ。
examples.reading: あといってんでごうかくだったとは、くやしいかぎりだ。
examples.en: To think I missed passing by one point: I could not be more frustrated.
examples.note: Negative feelings work too, as long as they are the speaker's own.

similarGrammar.difference: Nouns like 光栄の至り, 感激の極み: the same utmost feeling, but they attach to nouns only.
Spoken-style "cannot bear"; usable with a wider range of feelings and sensations.
Different word: "as long as / to the extent that" (私の知る限り). Not an intensifier.

commonMistakes.right: 彼は嬉しそうだ / 嬉しくてたまらないようだ。
commonMistakes.why: かぎりだ expresses only the speaker's own emotion; for a third person use そうだ / ようだ.

commonMistakes.wrong: この料理は美味しいかぎりだ。
commonMistakes.right: この料理は本当に美味しい。
commonMistakes.why: かぎりだ takes emotion adjectives, not descriptive ones like 美味しい or 大きい.
光栄 is a noun / な-adjective, so の (or な) is required before かぎり.

usageNotes: Frequent partners: 嬉しい, 寂しい, 羨ましい, 心強い, 悔しい, 恥ずかしい, 残念な, 光栄の.
Because it is the speaker's own feeling, the subject is normally omitted.
Fits acceptance speeches and thank-you letters; too formal for texting friends.
jlptTips: If the blank follows an emotion adjective and the sentence is a formal comment by the speaker, かぎりだ is the answer.
Distractors include 極まりない (which takes negative na-adjectives such as 失礼), ばかりだ ("only getting more"), and 限りは ("as long as").
A third-person subject rules out かぎりだ; look for そうだ / ようだ instead.
